tagline.text: A big water park in Clark Freeport with 38 slides and a wave pool

location.label: Location
location.text: Jose P. Rizal Avenue, Clark Freeport Zone, Mabalacat, Pampanga

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,800–2,800 (per person per day, including admission, locker and meals; transport not included)

children.text: Aqua Planet is one of the largest water parks in the Philippines, built on about 10 hectares in the northwest of Clark Freeport Zone. With high-thrill slides such as the Tornado and the Aqua Loop, a wave pool and a children's zone, it makes a good full day for families and friends alike.
Aqua Planet is a water park in the northwest of Clark Freeport Zone, which spans the city of Mabalacat in Pampanga. After a soft opening in November 2017, it officially opened on
February 24, 2018

. On about 10 hectares it offers 38 attractions, including slides and children's facilities. The rides were designed by an international aquatic design firm, and the park can handle several thousand guests at a time. It is run by a joint venture led by BB International and opened as the first phase of a large resort project of about
122ha

. The water is managed by four filtration systems, and most staff are reported to be trained as lifeguards. Height and weight limits on each slide are strict, though, so check beforehand who in your group can ride what to avoid surprises at the park.

The biggest draws are the Tornado, where rafts swing up and down the walls of a giant funnel; the Aqua Loop, which drops almost vertically before whipping through a 360-degree loop; and fast slides such as the Super Bowl and Sky Shuttle. There is also a large wave pool that produces eight kinds of waves, the slow-moving Wave River and a surf-style Flow Rider, so thrill seekers and relaxers can each play the way they like.

A separate Kiddie Zone for children under 122 cm (4 ft) makes the park popular with families. Mermaid Bay, Orc Lagoon and Bubble Base, a children's wave pool, are the main shallow-water areas, and an adult must stay with the children. Admission is priced by height, not by age.

The wristband you receive at the entrance, called the Planet Band, works as your ticket, locker key and e-wallet all in one. The park does not accept cash inside, so you load money onto the band and get the unused balance refunded when you leave. It is only about 10 minutes by car from Clark International Airport, so it fits easily into a half-day or full-day Clark itinerary.
This is the signature ride, where several people share a large raft that swings up and down the walls of a funnel. It is the ride visitors mention most often, and the speed can leave you dizzy.
This slide drops almost vertically from a tall tower and then runs through a full 360-degree loop. With a minimum height of about
152 cm
(5 ft), it has the strictest requirements and is the most thrilling attraction in the park.
You ride a raft around a giant bowl-shaped section or down a steep drop. Moments close to weightlessness make these the next most popular rides after the Tornado.
You slide headfirst on a mat down several lanes at once. You can start together with your group and race each other, which suits a trip with friends.
The large wave pool of about 3,500 sq m offers eight kinds of waves, while Boogie Bay and the Flow Rider let you try surf-style play. Some of these facilities have height and weight limits.
This is a lazy river where you float slowly around on a tube. It is a good place to rest after a few slides, and children and adults can ride it together.
Mermaid Bay, Orc Lagoon, Bubble Base and other shallow, safe water play areas are gathered here. It is for children under 122 cm only, and an accompanying adult is required.

Cabanas are rented separately from admission and come with cushions, a mist fan and a safe, which suits large families and groups. Shaded chairs and tables are first come, first served. For a family gathering or company outing, renting one gives you a base to leave your belongings and rest.

items.title: One-Day Plan
items.subtitle: Making the most of the day from opening time

children.text: Arrive at the entrance and join the line. If you arrive before opening and take care of your locker and Planet Band top-up in advance, the rest of the day goes more smoothly.
Right after opening, head first to the Tornado, Super Bowl and Sky Shuttle at the back of the park. Lines are short in the morning.
Have lunch. The food area is busiest between 12:00 and 1:30 PM, so it is better to eat a little earlier or later.
Cool off and rest at the Wave Pool and Wave River. If you are with children, spend the time in the Kiddie Zone.
Ride the remaining slides once more, and before closing collect your remaining Planet Band balance at the refund counter.

Last entry and closing times change by date, so check the official channels before you go. You leave your footwear at the bottom of the slide towers before climbing, and when lines are long a single ride can take more than 30 minutes, so deciding the order of the rides you want most will save time.
Let the kids get used to the water at Mermaid Bay and Bubble Base in the Kiddie Zone.
Have a simple meal for the children and rest in a shaded chair.
Ride the Wave River together and float slowly around. The park lends life jackets.
If the children are up for it, try one or two slides they are tall enough for, then call it a day.

If your child is close to 122 cm, staff may measure their height at the entrance, so bring an ID along with a document proving the child's age. Prices and free-entry rules for infants can differ by period, so check in advance.

Because this is a water park, it is best to visit in the dry season. From November to May there is little rain and the weather is stable, so you worry less about your plans falling through.

In March to May, however, midday temperatures are very high and the concrete gets hot underfoot, so bring aqua shoes or sandals. Weekdays are much quieter than weekends, so go on a weekday if your schedule allows.

and may vary with local conditions.
There is no lodging inside the park. Clark Freeport Zone has upscale hotels such as Midori Clark Hotel and Casino, Hilton Clark Sun Valley Resort and Clark Marriott, at around
a night. Mid-range hotels and guesthouses in Angeles and Mabalacat can be found for about
. Book early for March to May and Holy Week.
Inside the park there are restaurants and stalls selling pizza, snacks and ice cream, at about

per person. Outside food is not allowed except medical and infant food. Pampanga is famous as the culinary capital of the Philippines, so in the evening try local dishes such as sisig around Balibago in Angeles.

If you lose the Planet Band you receive on entry, you will be charged, and a band that has not been registered gets no protection for the money loaded on it. Register it at the guest service counter and look after it carefully.
Cash does not work inside the park. The reloading machines do not give change, so load only what you need and collect the remaining balance at the refund counter when you leave.
Eyeglasses, jewelry, denim, swimwear with metal fittings, mobile phones, cameras and selfie sticks cannot be taken onto the slides. Wear synthetic swimwear or a rash guard suitable for water play.
The weight limit is generally about
. Guests over the limit cannot ride the slides and are reported to receive a small merchandise voucher instead. Some attractions also have a minimum weight.
Arrive at opening time and start with the slides at the back of the park, where lines are much shorter. The food area is busiest at lunchtime.
Bring your own towel, sunscreen, hat and a change of clothes. Apply sunscreen about
30 minutes
before entering.
Drones are banned because of the airport's flight paths. Pets, personal tubes, folding chairs, tents and large umbrellas are also not allowed.
Senior and disability discounts are reported to be available at the ticket booth with an ID, but they may not combine with online bookings, so check first.

On weekends and holidays, lines for popular slides can run from 30 minutes to over an hour. Go on a weekday if you can; on a weekend, ride the slides in a concentrated burst right after opening and around lunchtime.

Cameras and phones cannot be used on the slides, so use a waterproof pouch only around the pools and put valuables in a locker. If you wear glasses, bring sports glasses with a strap or prescription swim goggles.
Operating days and hours, and the temporary closure of some attractions for maintenance, vary by period. Always check the official channels before you go.
Several guides list weekday hours of about
and weekend and holiday hours of
, but in the low season the park may close on certain days or shut facilities such as the wave pool for maintenance.
Using the slides is not recommended for anyone who is pregnant, has recently had surgery, or has neck, back or heart conditions.
Re-entry is not allowed, so sort out what you need before you leave. The park is not responsible for lost or damaged belongings.
Do not buy a cheap ticket from an outside site just because it looks like a bargain. Very low prices on some booking sites may not be a full admission ticket, so check what is included.
Height and weight limits are strictly enforced, so measuring your child beforehand can spare you disappointment at the park.
The area where the park stands, with the airport, casinos, hotels and shopping malls. It is around
10 minutes
away by car.
A drive-through wildlife safari and activity facilities make it a good pairing for the same day.
Korean restaurants and Korean shops are clustered here, convenient for dinner and shopping.
